result.title: Competition Domains Matter: Selective Head Globalization for Training-Free Sparse Attention in Video Diffusion Transformers
result.summary: Training-free sparse attention is a practical route to efficient video diffusion transformer inference, yet existing methods typically fix the competition domain at each query row for every attention head. Prior work primarily addresses how to estimate token-level importance within this fixed domain; whether the domain itself should adapt to head heterogeneity remains under-specified. We introduce EG-Sparse, a training-free framework that routes low-entropy heads to a grouped cross-head pool while retaining per-row local selection for high-entropy heads, using only scores already materialized by the sparse pipeline. A controlled diagnostic fixes the ranking score and varies only the competition rule: grouped cross-head selection reduces low-entropy-head reconstruction error by 9.8%, whereas forcing high-entropy heads into an all-head global pool increases it by 7.9%. Across four configurations, EG-Sparse achieves higher video quality while reducing attention density and GPU denoising latency compared with strong training-free sparse-attention baselines. Mechanism ablations further show that selective domain adaptation outperforms uniform, random, and fixed domain-assignment policies. These results support competition-domain adaptation as a distinct design axis within centroid-guided training-free sparse attention.

AI.brief_summary: 提出免训练稀疏注意力框架 EG-Sparse，按注意力头熵值把低熵头路由到跨头分组竞争池、高熵头保留逐行局部选择，仅用稀疏流程已有分数；在视频扩散 Transformer 上以诊断实验和四种配置表明该竞争域自适应可提升视频质量并降低注意力密度与去噪延迟。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「竞争域」设定与按头熵值差异化路由 token 选择的机制，可能为 LVR 中视觉证据筛选范围和注意力结构对 latent 相似度的影响提供可核查线索，但该工作面向视频扩散生成效率，与多模态推理状态的关联需人工判断。
